correctness.rationale: The strict-majority/tie-subset formula is an exact equivalence to the stated Markov support. The general hub condition forces two strict opposite bloc majorities and a central tie; therefore its closed four-state class, period two and fair-tie invariant distribution follow by a direct transition calculation. The complete finite n=2..5 claim is verified on all connected labelled graph masks by two independently coded transition relations and two SCC algorithms, and the canonical orbit sizes are derived by enumeration of all vertex permutations. Output 135=60+60+15, and no larger class exists in the exhaustive domain. No finite test is substituted for the analytical general lemma.

value.rationale: The smallest connected social network on which independent majority-tie coins enlarge the absorbing communication set beyond two configurations is a natural sharp threshold between the known cycle case and large-graph exponential constructions. The exact first-layer classification resolves existence, scarcity, and all graph topologies at onset, while the general balanced-hub inequalities identify a mechanistic cause of persistent stochastic disagreement. This is stronger than another unmotivated small graph example; it is an exact natural cutoff and complete first layer.
